Fast-Burn Alert (page): 14.4x burn over 1h (2% of budget) — page on-call
Slow-Burn Alert (ticket): 3x burn over 6h (5% of budget) — page on-call; 1x burn over 3 days — create ticket
Paging Threshold / Rule: Page if either fast-burn or slow-burn (6h) alert fires; ticket only for 3-day burn
Notes: Primary user-facing SLO; drives the availability conversation with the business

Definition (good / total events): Successful POST /checkout completions / total POST /checkout attempts (excluding payment-gateway-declined)
Slow-Burn Alert (ticket): 3x burn over 6h — page on-call; 1x over 3 days — ticket
Paging Threshold / Rule: Page on fast or slow burn as above
Notes: Checkout is the revenue path so it carries a stricter target than the API overall; PAYMENT_PENDING reconciliations count as success once confirmed within 15 min

Definition (good / total events): GET requests served in <= 300 ms / total GET requests
Fast-Burn Alert (page): p95 > 600 ms for 15 min — page on-call
Paging Threshold / Rule: Page on sustained p95 breach (15 min); ticket on 6h trend
Notes: Measured at the ALB so it includes network inside AWS; client-side latency monitored separately as an SLI-lite dashboard

Definition (good / total events): Write requests served in <= 800 ms / total write requests
Fast-Burn Alert (page): p95 > 1500 ms for 15 min — page on-call
Paging Threshold / Rule: Page on sustained p95 breach (15 min); ticket on 6h trend
Notes: Writes include DB commit + payment call; payment gateway time is included deliberately so gateway slowness is visible

Definition (good / total events): Catalogue price/stock changes visible via API within 60 s of DB commit / total changes sampled
Data Source: Synthetic probe (canary write + read every 5 min)
Error Budget (per window): 1% of sampled changes may be stale beyond 60 s
Notes: Freshness is a correctness guardrail for the Redis cache-aside design; stale-serve failure mode F7 is bounded by this SLI

Definition (good / total events): Orders confirmed in DB and present after any single-AZ failure / total confirmed orders (verified in quarterly restore test)
Fast-Burn Alert (page): Any order lost in restore test — page + incident
Slow-Burn Alert (ticket): Any backup job failure — ticket (page if 2 consecutive failures)
Paging Threshold / Rule: Page immediately on restore-test data loss
Notes: Verified by the quarterly restore drill (ADR-002); automated backup success is monitored daily as a supporting metric

Definition (good / total events): Successful automatic failover in game-day / failovers attempted
Fast-Burn Alert (page): Failover > 120 s or failed — incident review
Notes: Keeps failure path F2/F3 honest; results feed the availability error-budget review
